test_title: PYST 45 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 29 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
"From childhood, Japanese people are taught to respect rules, value punctuality, and prioritise community welfare over individual interests."

What is the **part of speech** of the word **"punctuality"?**
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3 (Noun)**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ***Option 1: Verb***

 
 
• This is **incorrect**. “Punctuality” does not denote an action; it names a quality.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Adjective***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The adjective form is “punctual,” not “punctuality.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Noun***
 
 
• This is **correct**. “Punctuality” is a noun that refers to the quality or state of being punctual (on time). In the sentence, it functions as the object of the verb “value.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Adverb***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The adverb form would be “punctually,” not “punctuality.”
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3 (Noun)**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Punctuality** is derived from the adjective *punctual* + suffix *-ity*, which forms abstract nouns denoting qualities.
 
• Examples: “responsible → responsibility,” “active → activity.”
 
• In the passage, “value punctuality” means to appreciate or respect the quality of being on time.
